phrasing_template: The long minute hand is pointing at the number {N}, and the short hour hand is pointing at the number {H}. What time does the clock show? Answer only in HH:MM format.
lead_ins_used: Here is a question about reading a clock.

conditions.matching_clock: real clock at H:(N*5 mod 60), clocks.generate_clock_image defaults
conditions.mismatched_clock: real clock at (H', M'): circular hour distance(H,H') >= 2; M' a multiple-of-5 minute whose clock number is at circular distance >= 3 from N; one draw per (N,H), seeded by image_seed

hour_hand_creep_note: matching_clock and mismatched_clock are REAL clocks drawn by clocks.generate_clock_image with default style: the hour hand creeps 0.5 deg per minute, so at large minute values it sits close to the NEXT hour number while the text says the hour hand points at H. Deliberate (dataset-style images); the minute is the headline metric.
chat_path: adapter.build_inputs(image_path_or_None, prompt) -> adapter.generate_answer(); identical call to eval_behavior.py (image first, then text)

adapter_notes.chat_template: Gemma3 turn format; <bos> comes from the template (tokenised via apply_chat_template, so no double BOS); no system prompt injected
adapter_notes.image: one image = 256 soft tokens (processor default, do_pan_and_scan False); processor also returns token_type_ids (1 = image) used for the bidirectional image-block mask in prefill
adapter_notes.decoding: greedy (do_sample=False), checkpoint sampling defaults top_k/top_p cleared, no repetition penalty (the checkpoint ships none)
adapter_notes.dtype: bfloat16 (default float16; env CLOCK_DTYPE=bfloat16|float32). Measured in notebook G0: float16 gives non-finite logits for gemma-3-4b-it and -12b-it on T4
